properties.statement:
REPORTED 2026-09-13 by flo2, relayed by @ajs. Not verified from flo2's side in this session.

WHAT CHANGED TODAY: flo2 declared reflow2's committed design export a watched dependency. flo2 now reads reflow2's facts routinely and, in its own words, "inherits the exposure in full."

WHY THAT MATTERS HERE AND NOT ONLY THERE. fact:the-retired-dependency-fact-misled-a-second-reader-2026-09-13 treated the stale-subject hazard as an internal reading problem — two readers of this graph reaching a wrong conclusion about this repo. It is no longer internal. A fact whose subject_id names a component this design has retired now travels out through the published export into a design that consumes it on a schedule. The blast radius of that class grew on the same day its second sighting was recorded, and the two facts were established hours apart.

THE RULE FLO2 PUT ON ITS OWN SIDE, recorded because it names the reflow2-side obligation by implication: "before citing a fact out of a mirrored design, check whether its subject is still a component that design holds." That is a discipline a consumer can follow only by reading BOTH designs. reflow2 is the side that knows when a subject left — see req:an-exported-fact-says-when-its-subject-left-the-design.

✅ THE WITHDRAWAL, KEPT VISIBLE RATHER THAN EDITED OUT, which is the right handling and is why it is written down: flo2 withdrew its claim that reflow2's design contradicts its code on the storage seam, re-read the ground from reflow2's source rather than from the bad fact, and restated item 3 as a feature request rather than a finding.

WHAT FLO2 CONFIRMED BY READING SOURCE — this is now grounded, unlike the citation it replaced:
  · KvBackend, MemoryBackend and RocksBackend are all pub(crate)
  · selection is by which constructor runs
  · rocksdb is an optional Cargo feature, and its ABSENCE MAKES open_rocksdb FAIL LOUD — not silently degrade
  · the CLI takes --graph-path and nothing naming a backend

⭐ THE FAIL-LOUD DETAIL IS THE ONE WORTH KEEPING. It rules out the failure mode dec:idea-is-the-byte-backend-selectable-at-runtime worried about from the compile-time side: a build without the feature does not quietly open an empty design, it refuses. Any runtime selector must preserve that property rather than reintroduce the silent-empty case.
